summary: Tenant requests guidance and help implementing a threshold-based fallback (granular deopt) for aggressive batching + quant profile
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (VerityAnalytics, dedicated) reports production regressions after enabling an aggressive combined configuration: batching_groups=auto aggressive, kv_prefetch=on, and a model quantization profile (int8 tuned for throughput). They want a tenant-scoped, threshold-driven deoptimization path (i.e., automatically scale back batching/quant settings when tenant p95 latency > threshold or error rate spikes) and help implementing it with minimal traffic disruption.

Impact:
- Multiple production applications of the customer observing tail-latency spikes and intermittent 5xx from serving-runtime during peak traffic windows (10:00-11:30 UTC).
- Business impact: slowed ingestion pipelines and elevated SLA alerts for two services; customer requests urgent assisted rollout for a safe fallback.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-03 (GPU: A10G mix)
- Models: redwood-13b-v2-quant (primary), redwood-7b-int8 (fallback variant)
- Traffic pattern: ~600 rps sustained with bursts to 1.2k rps

Steps to reproduce (from customer's dev-run):
1) Pin tenant to quant profile: throughput-optimized-int8
2) Enable aggressive batching_groups=auto with batch_timeout=8ms and kv_prefetch=on
3) Replay recorded traffic at 800 rps for 20 minutes
4) Observe p95 latency climb and occasional 503s

Observed behaviour:
- p95 latency increased from ~120ms to ~520ms under sustained bursts
- Intermittent 5xx from serving-runtime (stack traces reference async-batch flush timeouts)
- KV cache eviction counters increased and prefix-match miss rates rose by ~4x

Expected behaviour:
- Smooth degradation: automatic per-tenant fallback to a less aggressive config (reduced batching size, disable kv_prefetch, switch to fallback quant or fp16) once latency or error thresholds are hit, with minimal dropped requests and clear telemetry.

Logs / Telemetry (provided by customer):
- Excerpted serving-runtime logs indicating batch flush deadlines exceeded (attached in comments).
- Traces: heavy tail on request queue time; CPU on p-server ~85% during incident window.

Attachments:
- customer_trace_20260310.zip (provided via shared S3 link)
comments: 2026-03-12 10:22 - Aisha Patel: Customer opened ticket and attached sample trace and config. They asked for an assisted runbook to avoid a full revert because they want to keep some of the throughput gains.
2026-03-12 13:05 - Liam O'Connor: Requested tenant logs and exact optimizer flags. Asked whether customer can run a controlled replay in a staging tenant for validation. Added label 'safe-fallback'.
2026-03-12 17:41 - VerityAnalytics (customer): Provided logs and confirmed they can run a canary test in staging but want step-by-step commands and a fast rollback plan for prod.

2026-03-13 09:12 - Liam O'Connor: Performed initial analysis and proposed threshold triggers: p95_latency > 300ms sustained for 3 mins OR 5xx_rate > 1% over 2 mins => demote batching_groups to conservative, disable kv_prefetch, switch model routing to redwood-7b-int8 for tail sampling. Asked SRE to prepare traffic-split plan.

2026-03-13 11:00 - SRE (Maya Rodriguez): Confirmed ability to implement per-tenant traffic-split and provided link to temporary canary playbook. Scheduled a 30-minute window to apply controlled rollout with customer.
2026-03-14 02:08 - Aisha Patel: Customer confirmed successful canary run in staging (no p95 spikes) and requested assistance to apply to prod during low-traffic hours.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Aggressive batching combined with int8 quantization and kv_prefetch increases scheduling jitter and causes queue timeouts under bursty workloads.
Hypothesis 2: KV prefetch increases memory pressure and causes eviction cascades that degrade sequence cache hit rates, amplifying backend work per request.
Telemetry checks performed: p95 latency, request queue time, batch sizes, kv cache hit/miss counters, GPU utilization, async-batch flush duration.
Initial finding: p95 latency correlates strongly with average batch formation time during spikes. When batch formation exceeds configured batch_timeout, flush timers cause uneven load spikes.
Related config discovered in tenant profile: batching_groups=auto, batch_timeout_ms=8, kv_prefetch=true, quant_profile=throughput-int8, routing_policy=pin; fallback routing not configured.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied (2026-03-14 03:30 UTC): Implemented tenant-scoped adaptive rules:
- Trigger thresholds: p95>300ms for 3min OR 5xx_rate>1% for 2min.
- Actions on trigger: set batching_groups=conservative, set batch_timeout_ms=20, disable kv_prefetch, update routing to prefer redwood-7b-int8 at 20% shadow then 100% if condition persists for 6min.
- Traffic split executed gradually (10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 minutes) with health checks between steps.

Result: p95 dropped back to ~140ms within the controlled rollout window and 5xxs subsided. No customer-visible request loss reported.

Permanent follow-up tasks scheduled:
- Add tenant-level automated rollback playbook to Confluence with commands and runbook checks (owner: Platform Ops).
- Create a runtime guardrail that can auto-demote only one optimization at a time to reduce oscillation (owner: Serving Runtime team).
- Instrument a stronger KV eviction alert tied to tenant behavior so preemptive demotion can occur before SLA breach (owner: Observability).
- Postmortem to be written if any recurrence occurs during next 14 days.
resolution: Workaround applied: tenant-scoped adaptive fallback rules and staged traffic split; follow-up tasks scheduled.
